name: route-price
description: Route and price for the two OPEN rows. The atlas's own discipline lets OPEN rows quote no numbers — what they owe instead is a route with falsifiers and prices with derivations. This repo is that debt, paid: one dossier per OPEN row (dtc-clock, choice-primitive), each with certificate criteria, milestones that name their own failure mode, and price lines whose arithmetic is re-derived by executable witnesses (the Landauer floor with ln2 re-derived by quadrature and k the exact SI constant; the choice-primitive toy — coherent branching with engineered invariance versus random programs, the no-cloning wall executed as a rephasing-covariance separation, and the certification toll re-invoiced from the epoch-3 postselection ledger). Since v0.2.0 the priced milestones executed by siblings are receipted: D1-M3/D1-M4 by dtc-clock (beat-keyed register, energy certificate), D2-M4 by dsic-noether (the Groves gauge group and its welfare-gap charge) — each execution backed by a cross-check witness of this repo (W-D echo identity and own reversible multiplier; W-E zero net work, the detuned W_0 closed form and the tariff table re-priced on the own netlist; W-F the charge closed form, gauge invariance and the off-gauge deviation, bitwise on BigInt rationals). The checker refuses any dossier that claims settledness — the only verdict this repo can express is OPEN-ROUTE — and law R7 rejects any execution whose cross-check witness does not exist and pass. Since v0.2.1 the refusal itself is machine-readable: the shape law R0 names unreadable rows (a missing or mistyped column) instead of crashing on them, and the renderer's rejection is a coded, structured error (DOSSIER_REJECTED with the violations by law).
